searchText: Fusaka-devnet-2 update: All nimbus and nimbusel nodes are offline / or producing orphaned blocks. Lots of reth nodes are struggling to peer up with other ELs. We are falling out of sync and the issue is known, our long range syncing is heavily dependent on light client which is OFF for this devnet because of the new fork digest changes. Should take a couple of days to be fully fixed are CLs dropping statusv1 support post FULU? <@&1367819082019377202> More generally, when a new version of a message (StatusV2, MetadataV3) is introduced in a fork, should/may clients stop supporting the previous one? For example, Prysm already does not support any more Blocks By Range V1. Or Metadata V1 i think we should keep things backward compatible, just in case some protocol uses something in a fairly critical sense. for example, we don't really need earliest available slot for now in fulu, to sync, the peer rotation and switching should suffice the column sync, hence we never cared to actually use statusV2 and to only serve statusV2 correctly imo, the usage of statusV1 -> statusV2 is fairly fast paced and rushed in a sense, atleast we should support the former for a while, for a few devnets atleast Whats the timeline for devnet-3? once we have 7907 repricings values set, we can set the timeline for devnet 3 after alpha.3 any estimates? i need to work some cleanups, optimizations meanwhile and not just the latest spec CL side there aren't any changes afaik for devnet 3 all the clarifications were already in devnet 2 oh ok thanks <@785811170387951616> <@531934490826768418> <@412614104222531604> Is it worth defining in the specifications when when StatusV1 is considered deprecated & is no longer expected to be used? We don't typically say this in the specs. I think we can drop StatusV1 support at the fork. i think we should either mention it in spec about the deprecation/ or wait a couple more releases to be fully deprecated as the change is literally 1 week old I don't really understand. It's not like we're deprecating V1 right now. Why does a couple more releases matter? i can't speak for other CLs but right now we are not really using statusV2 to sync, and to fully utilise earliest available slot from status v2 in our sync mechanism, we need a bit more time imo, 2 releases worth of time atleast which is why i'm suggesting to proceed with v1 deprecation to be a bit gradual > It's not like we're deprecating V1 right now there are a few cls that i can notice that aren't agreeing on v1 post fulu in the devnet, <@531934490826768418> agreed that prysm doesn't So this is just a current devnet issue. since, it's been raised, yes and since it's visible

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content:
Fusaka-devnet-2 update:

All nimbus and nimbusel nodes are offline / or producing orphaned blocks.
Lots of reth nodes are struggling to peer up with other ELs.

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content:
We are falling out of sync and the issue is known, our long range syncing is heavily dependent on light client which is OFF for this devnet because of the new fork digest changes.

Should take a couple of days to be fully fixed

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: are CLs dropping statusv1 support post FULU? <@&1367819082019377202>

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: More generally, when a new version of a message (StatusV2, MetadataV3) is introduced in a fork, should/may clients stop supporting the previous one?

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: For example, Prysm already does not support any more Blocks By Range V1.

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: Or Metadata V1

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: i think we should keep things backward compatible, just in case some protocol uses something in a fairly critical sense. for example, we don't really need earliest available slot for now in fulu, to sync, the peer rotation and switching should suffice the column sync, hence we never cared to actually use statusV2 and to only serve statusV2 correctly

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: imo, the usage of statusV1 -> statusV2 is fairly fast paced and rushed in a sense, atleast we should support the former for a while, for a few devnets

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: atleast

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: <@785811170387951616> <@531934490826768418> <@412614104222531604> Is it worth defining in the specifications when when StatusV1 is considered deprecated & is no longer expected to be used? We don't typically say this in the specs. I think we can drop StatusV1 support at the fork.

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: i think we should either mention it in spec about the deprecation/ or wait a couple more releases to be fully deprecated as the change is literally 1 week old

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: I don't really understand. It's not like we're deprecating V1 right now. Why does a couple more releases matter?

excerpts.author: agnxsh

excerpts.author: agnxsh
